spans.s:
Aitareya, perhaps a patronymic from Itara, though the commentator Sāyaṇa regards the word as a metronymic from Itarā, is an epithet of Mahidāsa in the aitareya Āraṇyaka and the Chāndogya upaniṣad.
Foot notes Cited by Aufrecht, aitareya brāhmaṇa, 3.
ii. 1, 8; 3. 7.
iii. 16, 7. Cf. Weber, Indische Studien, 1, 389. The form Aitareyin occurs in the Anupada sūtra, viii. 1; Āśvalāyana Srauta sūtra, i. 3, etc.; and a mahaitareya in Āśvalāyana gṛhya sūtra, iii. 4, 4, etc.

Aitaśa, Aitaśāyana. See etaśa, Etaśāyana. The Aitaśapralāpa, or ‘Discourse of aitaśa,’ is a part of the Atharvaveda.
Foot notes xx. 129-132. Cf. Bṛhaddevatā, viii. 101, with Macdonell's note.
